posts.linkedin:
Many small business owners spend hours writing reel scripts that never get posted.

It often happens late in the evening. A doctor, a boutique owner, or a gym coach decides to record a short video for social media. They open a notes app and write fifteen full sentences. When the camera turns on they try to read every line verbatim. The delivery feels stiff, they stumble, and after many retakes the video is abandoned. The result is a lot of wasted effort and missed opportunities to connect with potential customers.

I provide short reel scripts in Hindi‑English or English that are meant to be spoken naturally. They are not formal marketing copy. Each script contains a three‑second hook that captures attention, a core message lasting thirty to sixty seconds, and a clear call to action at the end. I adapt the wording to match the way you normally speak, so the final video feels authentic.

The process is simple. First you tell me what your business sells and the most common questions customers ask. I then turn that information into three spoken prompts instead of a dense paragraph. For example: line one states the daily problem, line two offers a practical fix, line three tells the viewer how to contact you. After I send the draft you can suggest edits, and I revise until the wording feels natural for you.

This structure can reduce the need for multiple retakes and may save hours of second‑guessing. Because you are speaking to the camera as if answering a customer standing in your shop, the language stays conversational and the video stays focused on what buyers care about. The concise format also keeps the video under a minute, which aligns with the attention span of many viewers. It can make regular content creation more realistic for busy owners.

A script cannot create confidence on its own or replace your product knowledge. It only provides a logical flow, a strong opening, and a clear ending. Think of the script as a guide that helps you stay on track, not a magic formula. You still need to record yourself and deliver the points in your own tone.

If you want a simpler way to record reels, DM SCRIPT.

spec.headline: The mistake of essay scripts versus simple prompts
spec.sub: Reading paragraphs freezes you. Three lines keep you natural.

alts: The mistake of writing a full essay instead of a 3-line prompt

Slide 2 of 7: What happens when you try to memorize a long script. You stare at the camera trying to recall sentences word for word. One slip means starting again, leaving you drained before you even post.
Slide 3 of 7: Brochure language does not sound natural on camera. When you read formal sentences, you sound like a printed brochure rather than an owner speaking directly to an everyday customer.
Slide 4 of 7: Switch to a simple three-part spoken framework. Instead of writing a full script, write just three clear lines: the customer's problem, your proof, and the direct action to take.
Slide 5 of 7: Speak in your natural everyday voice. Use simple Hinglish or conversational English. When you talk naturally like you do in your daily work, your confidence comes through immediately.

Slide 6 of 7: Record comfortably without memorizing entire paragraphs. Glancing at three bullet points lets you speak smoothly in one take. It saves valuable time and makes filming reels much more relaxed.
Slide 7 of 7: DM SCRIPT. Message me to discuss simple reel scripts for your business. We can chat about what fits your daily workflow.
